correctness.rationale: The sharp squared evaluation bound in averaged L² on [-1,1] is 1+3x² for each fixed real |x|≥1. Removing the midpoint carrier, cosine and sine at half the gap d are orthogonal with squared average norms (1±s)/2, s=sin(d)/d. Their evaluation contributions add to 2(1−s cos(dx))/(1−s²), including for complex coefficients. For d≥2, |s|<1/2 (strict also at d=2), so the kernel is <4. For 0<d<2, s>0 and the cosine quadratic lower bound gives K≤1+(1−s)/(1+s)+sd²x²/(1−s²). For u=d² and q=1−s, the combined coefficient of x² after using x²≥1 is <3 precisely when 6q−4q²−(1−q)u>0. On u/6−u²/120≤q≤u/6, its q-derivative is ≥2/3+u and its value at the lower endpoint is u²(20+10u−u²)/3600>0. This proves strictness for every distinct pair, including |x|=1. A single wave gives 1. The confluent sequence cos(ht)+3x sin(ht)/h tends uniformly on the required compact set to 1+3xt, whose averaged squared norm and value at x both equal 1+3x²; hence the supremum is exact and unattained.
residual_risks: Replay is a finite floating-point check; universality follows from the analytic comparison. No claim of the same formula in the interior or for three waves.
